entry.title: Schiansky et al. 2023 · Supplementary Note 3B
entry.subtitle: P04 · Nat. Commun. 14, 3849 (published 2023-06-29; corrected 2023-08-21). Read after correction.
entry.summary: Analytic fit to the optimal cheating boundary: e = -(1/(4+2 sqrt2)) l + (1 - p_m/2)/(8 + 4 sqrt2) (16).
entry.anchor: Supplementary Note 3B, eqs.(16)-(18), SI PDF p.6-7; main text Fig.4a

fields.label: Anchor
fields.text: Supplementary Note 3B, eqs.(16)-(18), SI PDF p.6-7; main text Fig.4a

fields.label: Statement summary
fields.text: Analytic fit to the optimal cheating boundary: e = -(1/(4+2 sqrt2)) l + (1 - p_m/2)/(8 + 4 sqrt2) (16). Equivalently, the secure region is M(e,l) = (4+2 sqrt2) e + l <= (1/2)(1 - p_m/2) (18). N -> infinity is justified 'following the exponential de Finetti arguments' (qualitative).

fields.label: Variables
fields.text:
e: fraction of declared outcomes that disagree with (b, B)
l: fraction of token states declared lost
p_m: multiphoton emission probability

fields.label: Recomputation
fields.text: RECOMPUTED_BY_LANE_A: e*(l=0.224) = 3.795% with p_m=6.76% (main-text value) and 3.822% with p_m=6.02% (SI Table 2 value). These match the main-text 3.79% and SI 3.82%. So the two documents use different p_m. Allowed mishaps M = 0.5(1-0.0602/2) = 0.48495 matches SI 0.4849.

fields.label: Caveats
items: eq.(16) is described as 'an analytical expression that fits' the SDP optimum. It's a fit, not a derived theorem.
Collective-to-coherent reduction (de Finetti) is argued, not quantified.
